subject: Request: Adjudication of 2028-03-14 checkout interruption and credit path

Date: 2028-03-14T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout spike and 39m outage (03/14) — confirmation & credits

Hi Olga,

We observed a ~39 minute interruption in checkout success rates this morning between 02:12–02:51 UTC (our monitoring shows 503s and timeouts against Redwood API). That period directly caused ~$24k in lost transactions for us and we need confirmation from Redwood on whether this window qualifies for SLA credit and an initial estimate of remedy.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood saw an availability gap in us-west-2 for our tenant during that window.
- What the next steps are for a credit calculation and postmortem.

We'd like the raw traces and per-route latency breakdown for that window (token-level traces if available). If you can acknowledge receipt and next steps timeline, we can escalate internally.

Thanks,

Date: 2028-03-14T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout spike and 39m outage (03/14) — confirmation & credits

Olga, team — quick update from telemetry:
- I pulled the RPC traces and instance logs for 02:00–03:15 UTC in us-west-2 for Halley tenant. There is a clear spike in 503s starting at 02:12 UTC coincident with an autoscaler eviction event (node preempt) at 02:09:47 UTC and a subsequent cold-start window while warmup completed.
- The error-rate window where customer traffic saw >=5% error-rate is 02:12:18–02:51:07 UTC (39m). I exported token-level traces and a consolidated trace bundle, see drive link (internal).
- No evidence of tenant misconfiguration or malformed requests from Halley. The root cause appears to be a combination of preemption + delayed cache warmup for the model variant they serve.

I'm attaching the trace bundle and a short telemetry summary (raw-traces-20280314.tar.gz, included in this thread). I'll produce a per-route latency CSV by EOD.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: raw-traces-20280314.tar.gz (trace bundle stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james.park@halleycommerce.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout spike and 39m outage (03/14) — confirmation & credits

Hi James / Halley team — thanks for flagging and for working with us while we investigated.

Summary & next steps:
- Redwood confirms an availability gap for Halley in us-west-2 between 2028-03-14T02:12:18Z and 2028-03-14T02:51:07Z (39 minutes) attributable primarily to a preemption-induced capacity shortfall and cache warmup lag as described by Karthik.
- Per Halley's contract (Standard Tier, monthly committed usage), the SLA provides a prorated credit for unavailability above our 99.9% SLA threshold. Preliminary calculation attached: billing-window-calculation-20280314.csv.
- Proposed remedy: 1) Issue a prorated service credit equal to 0.5x of one day's average invoice for the affected month (provisional until final adjudication), 2) Schedule joint postmortem on 2028-03-18 (invite attached), 3) Karthik to deliver a remediation plan for autoscaler warmup and preemption handling within 7 business days.

Please confirm acceptance of the provisional credit path so we can route for billing approval. If Halley prefers a different credit calculation (prorate by minutes rather than a 0.5x provisional), let us know and we will recompute.

Apologies for the impact — we will include corrective controls to reduce probability of recurrence.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Billing & Contracts
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: billing-window-calculation-20280314.csv; postmortem-invite-20280318.ics
